findings.title: External straight-path overlay
findings.claim: When the explicitly added path language is brought in after the native pericope, the focus's service contrast can be pictured as distinct courses: a road made passable and straight, with the danger of a course whose traveler is lost.
findings.mechanism: The focus road, dispersed-course, and stranded-carrier facets meet the exact external path occurrences at 1:6:2 and 1:7:1, the external difference marker at 1:7:5, and the lost-course occurrence at 1:7:9; the contact adds direction and danger beyond the native pass image.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus distinction gains a directional picture in which allegiance is a course and the central danger is losing its guidance, while the external material remains an overlay rather than the starting frame.
findings.containment: Only the bounded path contact is retained. The added Fātiḥa material does not establish a whole-surah path system, make the focus words literal roads or animals, or replace the native worship contrast.

epistemic.reason: The external context supplies exact root occurrences and path cues, and the focus branches are registered, but no authored support or trust label accompanies this uncandidate overlay.
